title: One commit and one push per step, instead of per record
description:
A single reconcile end-to-end test performs 87 pushes: every durable record is its own commit AND its own push. In tests that is process cost; in production each push is a network round-trip to origin - and the network is where this run lost two and a half hours to a git fetch holding an ssh connection open with no bound.

Batching a step's records into one commit and one push would cut process count, wall clock and network exposure together. It is the largest single win in this epic.

It is also the one that changes MEANING, which is why it is its own tick and blocked on the plumbing work. Today each record lands separately and the compare-and-swap guarantees are stated per record; a batched commit changes what is atomic and what a resumed run sees when it reads a partially-written step. Do not start by writing code: start by stating which invariants the current per-record commits provide (Appendix A, the CAS rules in .ticfac/), which of them a per-step commit preserves, and which need a different mechanism. If any invariant cannot survive it, say so and stop - a faster run that loses a durability guarantee is not the trade this epic wants.
acceptance_criteria: A step's records reach origin as one commit and one push where the invariants allow it, with the analysis of which invariants were checked recorded on the tick. A resumed run reads a batched step correctly, including a run killed mid-step, and a test covers that. Push count for the same fixture epic drops materially (report before and after). No compare-and-swap guarantee is weakened without an explicit decision recorded here.
